data.name: Aaeedah
data.gender_notes: Aaeedah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aaeedah is a name of Arabic origin that means 'servant of Allah'. It is a Quranic name, derived from the root letters 'AA-AA-DA' which are found in various verses in the Quran. The name Aaeedah carries the meaning “Servant of Allah” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aaeedah usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of allah and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A constant reminder to stay devoted to Allah and fulfill the duties that come with being a servant of the Almighty.
data.etymology: Aaeedah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant of Allah.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaeedah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

During the Ridda Wars, which were a series of military campaigns launched by Muhammad and his followers to re-establish Islamic rule in the Arabian Peninsula after the hijrah (migration to Medina), a woman named Aaeedah bint Ar-Rabee' Ibn Umaiyah al-Qurashiya stood out for her bravery and leadership. She led a group of women to defend Medina against the forces of the tribal leader Harith ibn Abi Shammas, and was instrumental in turning the tide of the battle in favor of the Muslims.
